\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} Indonesia CVD model engine (\texttt{06\_run\_scenarios\_indonesia\_fair.R}). \textbf{Method:} interventions act on two transitions --- new cases (Healthy $\rightarrow$ Living with CVD) and the risk of dying after developing CVD (Living with CVD $\rightarrow$ death); no recovery/remission is modelled, a conservative assumption.}

# The interventions we tested

## Clinical care prevents disease and helps people survive it

```{r tbl-clin-interventions, results='asis'}
## Built from the ACTIVE clinical scenarios in this run (children/aggregate
## excluded); target-population / effect notes come from a small presentation map.
clin_pop <- c(
  I_CVD_PRIMARY = "Adults at cardiovascular risk", I_T2D_TREATMENT = "People with type-2 diabetes",
  I_IHD_SECONDARY = "Heart-attack (IHD) survivors", I_STROKE_SECONDARY = "Stroke survivors",
  I_HF_CHRONIC = "Chronic heart-failure patients", I_HF_ACUTE = "Acute heart-failure patients",
  I_RHD_SECONDARY = "Rheumatic heart disease patients")
clin_acts <- c(I_CVD_PRIMARY = "\\textcolor{incidencecol}{Fewer new cases}")
clin_disp <- top_level_rows(met_clin, clin_all_id)[scenario != clin_all_id]
if (nrow(clin_disp)) {
  pluck <- function(vec, key, default) if (key %in% names(vec)) vec[[key]] else default
  cd <- data.table(
    Intervention = vapply(clin_disp$scenario, function(s) lbl(s, met_clin), character(1)),
    Population   = vapply(clin_disp$scenario, function(s) pluck(clin_pop, s, "Target patient group"), character(1)),
    Acts         = vapply(clin_disp$scenario, function(s)
                     pluck(clin_acts, s, "\\textcolor{casefatalcol}{Better survival}"), character(1)))
  print(kbl(cd, format="latex", booktabs=TRUE, escape=FALSE,
      col.names=c("Intervention","Target population","Model effect"), align="lll") |>
    kable_styling(latex_options="hold_position", font_size=8.5) |>
    column_spec(1, bold=TRUE, width="4.6cm") |>
    column_spec(2, width="6.4cm") |> column_spec(3, width="3.0cm") |>
    row_spec(0, bold=TRUE))
  reg_tbl("tbl-clin-interventions",
          "Clinical care prevents disease and helps people survive it",
          cd, c("Intervention", "Target population", "Model effect"))
} else cat("\\begin{center}\\large No clinical interventions selected for this run.\\end{center}")
```

\vspace{2pt}
\footnotesize \textbf{Implementation scenario (all clinical interventions):} coverage scales up \textbf{from a low base toward 80\%} of the people who need each service between `r HZ_START` and `r HZ_END`. Primary prevention lowers who develops CVD (new cases); secondary prevention and treatment improve survival.

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} clinical results workbook, sheets \texttt{Selected\_Interventions} and \texttt{Scenario\_Catalog}. \textbf{Method:} the table lists the clinical interventions active in this run (excluded interventions never appear); effect sizes come from the FAIR Choices intervention taxonomy.}

```{r tbl-ph-interventions, results='asis'}
            "Reformulation, labelling, media, procurement","Best-practice industrial TFA ban",
            "Mandatory reformulation","Front-of-pack labelling","Mass-media campaign","Public-institution environment",
            "Smoke-free / clean-air law","Mass-media campaign","Advertising ban"))
ph_disp <- top_level_rows(met_ph, ph_all_id)[scenario != ph_all_id]
if (nrow(ph_disp)) {
  pd <- merge(ph_disp[, .(scenario)], ph_meta, by = "scenario", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
  pd[, Policy := vapply(scenario, function(s) lbl(s, met_ph), character(1))]
  pd[is.na(Risk),  Risk  := "Behavioural risk factor"]
  pd[is.na(Acts),  Acts  := "\\textcolor{incidencecol}{New cases}"]
  pd[is.na(Lever), Lever := "Fiscal / regulatory measure"]
  print(kbl(pd[, .(Policy, Risk, Acts, Lever)], format="latex", booktabs=TRUE, escape=FALSE,
      col.names=c("Policy","Risk factor","Model effect","Implementation lever"), align="llll") |>
    kable_styling(latex_options="hold_position", font_size=7.8) |>
    column_spec(1, bold=TRUE, width="2.9cm") |> column_spec(2, width="2.3cm") |>
    column_spec(3, width="3.1cm") |> column_spec(4, width="5.7cm") |>
    row_spec(0, bold=TRUE))
  reg_tbl("tbl-ph-interventions",
          "Population policies cut tobacco, salt, and trans-fat risk across the whole population",
          pd[, .(Policy, Risk, Acts, Lever)],
          c("Policy", "Risk factor", "Model effect", "Implementation lever"))
} else cat("\\begin{center}\\large No public-health policies selected for this run.\\end{center}")
```

\vspace{1pt}
\footnotesize Policies reduce exposure (smoking, salt, trans-fat intake), lowering the number of \textbf{new CVD cases}. \textbf{Tobacco} policies additionally improve \textbf{survival} after CVD. Packages are modelled as single joint runs of their component measures.

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} public-health results workbook, sheets \texttt{Selected\_Interventions} / \texttt{Policy\_Levers} and \texttt{Scenario\_Catalog}. \textbf{Method:} the table lists the policies active in this run; effect sizes come from published risk-factor evidence stored in the workbook.}

## Costs depend on who needs care, how many receive it, and local prices

\footnotesize We estimate the \textbf{additional health-system resources required to expand effective coverage}, using a costing approach adapted from Disease Control Priorities (DCP) [@Watkins2020ResourceRequirements].

<!-- \footnotesize We estimate costs with an intervention-based approach adapted from the Disease Control Priorities (DCP) cost model of @Watkins2020ResourceRequirements, applied here from a \textbf{health-system perspective} with \textbf{annual} projections. Each service is costed as: \emph{who needs it} $\times$ \emph{how much of that need is met} $\times$ \emph{services per person per year} $\times$ \emph{Indonesia-adjusted unit cost}. -->

\vspace{2pt}
\begin{center}
\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
\begin{tikzpicture}[
   >=Latex, node distance = 5mm, font=\scriptsize,
   costbox/.style = {rectangle, rounded corners, draw=wbnavy, thick, fill=wbnavy!6,
                  text width=22mm, minimum height=14mm, align=center},
   costout/.style = {rectangle, rounded corners, draw=clinicalcol, very thick, fill=clinicalcol!8,
                  text width=27mm, minimum height=14mm, align=center}]
  \node[costbox] (pin)  {\textbf{People who need}\\ the service};
  \node[costbox, right=of pin] (cov) {\textbf{Current coverage}\\ \& scale-up target};
  \node[costbox, right=of cov] (freq){\textbf{Services}\\ per person / year};
  \node[costbox, right=of freq] (uc) {\textbf{Indonesia unit}\\ cost};
  \node[costbox, right=of uc] (ann) {\textbf{Annual cost}\\ baseline \& scenario};
  \node[costout,  right=of ann] (res){\textbf{Additional \& discounted cost;} cost per person; cost per death prevented};
  \draw[->,thick] (pin)--(cov); \draw[->,thick] (cov)--(freq); \draw[->,thick] (freq)--(uc);
  \draw[->,thick] (uc)--(ann);  \draw[->,thick, clinicalcol] (ann)--(res);
\end{tikzpicture}}
\end{center}

\vspace{2pt}
<!-- \footnotesize The DCP paper supplies the \textbf{conceptual framework} --- unit costs, demographic/epidemiological estimates of the people in need, baseline coverage, and health-system delivery costs. This project \textbf{adapts} that framework to Indonesia and does not claim to reproduce the paper exactly. -->

\footnotesize\textbf{What this tells policymakers:} the analysis estimates how much additional health-system spending is required to move from today's coverage toward universal, high-quality access—and relates that investment to the health gains achieved.

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} intervention-based costing adapted from Watkins et al. (2020); unit costs and coverage from the input workbooks; demography from UN WPP 2024. \textbf{Method:} annual cost = people in need $\times$ coverage $\times$ annual service frequency $\times$ Indonesia-adjusted unit cost; additional cost = scenario minus baseline; equations in the appendix. \costcaveat}

# What the interventions deliver, and at what cost

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} clinical cost workbook (\texttt{indonesia\_model\_cost\_value\_formulae.xlsx}, sheet \texttt{Budget\_Impact}); population is the workbook's own \texttt{national\_population}. \textbf{Method:} cost per death averted $=$ discounted additional cost $\div$ deaths averted (`r fmt_pct(disc_rate*100,0)`/yr, `r price_year` US\$, `r cost_perspective`). \textbf{Avg. annual additional cost per capita, 2026--`r HZ_END`} $=$ cumulative discounted additional cost over 2026--`r HZ_END` $\div$ (25 $\times$ `r HZ_START+1L` population). \textbf{Additional cost per capita in `r HZ_END`} $=$ discounted additional cost in `r HZ_END` $\div$ `r HZ_END` population. \costcaveat}

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} clinical cost workbook (\texttt{indonesia\_model\_cost\_value\_formulae.xlsx}, sheet \texttt{Budget\_Impact}); population is the workbook's own \texttt{national\_population}. \textbf{Method (undiscounted):} cost per death averted $=$ \textbf{undiscounted} additional cost $\div$ deaths averted (`r price_year` US\$, `r cost_perspective`). \textbf{Avg. annual additional cost per capita, 2026--`r HZ_END`} $=$ cumulative \textbf{undiscounted} additional cost over 2026--`r HZ_END` $\div$ (25 $\times$ `r HZ_START+1L` population). \textbf{Additional cost per capita in `r HZ_END`} $=$ \textbf{undiscounted} additional cost in `r HZ_END` $\div$ `r HZ_END` population. Health results are identical to the discounted slide. \costcaveat}

```{r clin-budget-data, include=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Clinical budget impact over time, decomposed by clinical intervention.
## Source of truth: the CLINICAL cost workbook (Annual_Cost) - the all-clinical
## scenario's discounted additional cost, keyed by (year, intervention_id), with
## the workbook's shared-cost rule (count each shared component once). Population
## is the workbook's own national_population. Two cumulative measures:
##   left  = cumulative DISCOUNTED total additional cost through year t
##   right = that cumulative total / national_population(t)  (per capita through t)
## QA: intervention-level totals must reconcile, by year, to the all-clinical
## Budget_Impact totals (annual and cumulative).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
.cb_ac <- read_clin_ac()
.cb_bi <- read_clin_bi()
need_ac <- c("scenario","year","intervention_id","disc_cost_incremental","shared_duplicate_count")
val_stop(all(need_ac %in% names(.cb_ac)), "clinical Annual_Cost missing a column needed for the budget figure")
val_stop("all" %in% .cb_ac$scenario, "clinical Annual_Cost has no all-clinical scenario for the budget figure")
.cb_ac[, w := 1 / pmax(shared_duplicate_count, 1)]     # shared components counted once
clin_bud <- .cb_ac[scenario == "all",
                   .(disc = sum(disc_cost_incremental * w)), by = .(intervention_id, year)]
setorder(clin_bud, intervention_id, year)
clin_bud[, cum := cumsum(disc), by = intervention_id]
clin_pop <- .cb_bi[scenario == "all", .(year, pop = national_population)]
clin_bud <- merge(clin_bud, clin_pop, by = "year")
clin_bud[, cum_pc := cum / pop]                        # cumulative discounted cost per capita through t

## QA reconciliation to the all-clinical Budget_Impact (annual + cumulative).
.qa_ann <- merge(clin_bud[, .(s = sum(disc)), by = year],
                 .cb_bi[scenario == "all", .(year, bi = disc_incremental_cost)], by = "year")
val_stop(max(abs(.qa_ann$s - .qa_ann$bi)) < 1,
         "clinical budget figure: intervention sums do not reconcile to all-clinical annual cost")
.qa_cum <- merge(clin_bud[, .(s = sum(cum)), by = year],
                 .cb_bi[scenario == "all", .(year, bic = cumulative_disc_incremental_cost)], by = "year")
val_stop(max(abs(.qa_cum$s - .qa_cum$bic)) < 1,
         "clinical budget figure: intervention sums do not reconcile to all-clinical cumulative cost")
val_stop(setequal(clin_bud$year, HZ_START:HZ_END), "clinical budget figure: year coverage is not 2025-2050")

## Plain-language labels + stacking order (largest cumulative contribution first).
.ord <- clin_bud[year == HZ_END, .(cum), by = intervention_id][order(-cum)]
.ord[, lab := vapply(intervention_id, function(s) lbl(s, met_clin), character(1))]
lev <- .ord$lab
clin_bud[, ivlab := vapply(intervention_id, function(s) lbl(s, met_clin), character(1))]
clin_bud[, ivlab := factor(ivlab, levels = rev(lev))]  # largest at bottom of the stack
## Accessible clinical palette (blue-anchored), one colour per intervention, shared across panels.
clin_bud_pal <- setNames(
  c("#08306B","#2171B5","#6BAED6","#B2182B","#EF8A62","#00897B","#66C2A5","#B39DDB")[seq_len(nrow(.ord))],
  .ord$lab)
## Long form: two panels.
cb_long <- rbind(
  clin_bud[, .(year, ivlab, value = cum / 1e9,
               panel = "Cumulative discounted additional cost (US$ billions)")],
  clin_bud[, .(year, ivlab, value = cum_pc,
               panel = "Cumulative discounted additional cost per capita (US$)")])
cb_long[, panel := factor(panel, levels = c("Cumulative discounted additional cost (US$ billions)",
                                            "Cumulative discounted additional cost per capita (US$)"))]
## Takeaway title (plain text; no % or $ so it survives \frametitle).
clin_top_lab   <- .ord$lab[1]
clin_top_share <- .ord$cum[1] / sum(.ord$cum) * 100
title_clin_budget <- sprintf(
  "%s drives most of Indonesia's clinical cardiovascular budget through %d",
  clin_top_lab, HZ_END)
```

```{r clin-budget-data-undisc, include=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## UNDISCOUNTED clinical budget impact over time -- an exact twin of clin-budget-data
## using the workbook's UNDISCOUNTED annual_cost_incremental (shared components counted
## once via the same w). Reuses the discounted figure's palette (clin_bud_pal) and
## stacking order (lev) so the two figures are visually comparable; only the monetary
## magnitudes differ. QA: intervention-level totals reconcile, by year, to the
## all-clinical Budget_Impact UNDISCOUNTED annual + cumulative totals.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
need_ac_u <- c("scenario","year","intervention_id","annual_cost_incremental")
val_stop(all(need_ac_u %in% names(.cb_ac)), "clinical Annual_Cost missing a column needed for the undiscounted budget figure")
clin_bud_u <- .cb_ac[scenario == "all",
                     .(undisc = sum(annual_cost_incremental * w)), by = .(intervention_id, year)]
setorder(clin_bud_u, intervention_id, year)
clin_bud_u[, cum := cumsum(undisc), by = intervention_id]
clin_bud_u <- merge(clin_bud_u, clin_pop, by = "year")     # clin_pop (national_population) from clin-budget-data
clin_bud_u[, cum_pc := cum / pop]                          # cumulative undiscounted cost per capita through t
## QA reconciliation to the all-clinical Budget_Impact UNDISCOUNTED annual + cumulative.
.qa_ann_u <- merge(clin_bud_u[, .(s = sum(undisc)), by = year],
                   .cb_bi[scenario == "all", .(year, bi = incremental_cost)], by = "year")
val_stop(max(abs(.qa_ann_u$s - .qa_ann_u$bi)) < 1,
         "undiscounted clinical budget figure: intervention sums do not reconcile to all-clinical annual cost")
.qa_cum_u <- merge(clin_bud_u[, .(s = sum(cum)), by = year],
                   .cb_bi[scenario == "all", .(year, bic = cumulative_incremental_cost)], by = "year")
val_stop(max(abs(.qa_cum_u$s - .qa_cum_u$bic)) < 1,
         "undiscounted clinical budget figure: intervention sums do not reconcile to all-clinical cumulative cost")
val_stop(setequal(clin_bud_u$year, HZ_START:HZ_END), "undiscounted clinical budget figure: year coverage is not 2025-2050")
clin_bud_u[, ivlab := vapply(intervention_id, function(s) lbl(s, met_clin), character(1))]
clin_bud_u[, ivlab := factor(ivlab, levels = rev(lev))]    # same stacking order + palette as the discounted figure
cb_long_u <- rbind(
  clin_bud_u[, .(year, ivlab, value = cum / 1e9,
                 panel = "Cumulative additional cost (US$ billions)")],
  clin_bud_u[, .(year, ivlab, value = cum_pc,
                 panel = "Cumulative additional cost per capita (US$)")])
cb_long_u[, panel := factor(panel, levels = c("Cumulative additional cost (US$ billions)",
                                              "Cumulative additional cost per capita (US$)"))]
.ord_u <- clin_bud_u[year == HZ_END, .(cum), by = intervention_id][order(-cum)]
.ord_u[, lab := vapply(intervention_id, function(s) lbl(s, met_clin), character(1))]
title_clin_budget_undisc <- sprintf(
  "%s still drives most of the undiscounted clinical cardiovascular budget through %d",
  .ord_u$lab[1], HZ_END)
```

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} clinical cost workbook (\texttt{indonesia\_model\_cost\_value\_formulae.xlsx}, sheet \texttt{Annual\_Cost}); all-clinical scenario, discounted additional cost by intervention (shared components counted once); population is the workbook's own \texttt{national\_population}. \textbf{Method:} `r HZ_START` is the discount base year and coverage scales up over `r HZ_START`--`r HZ_END`; left is cumulative discounted additional cost through each year, right is that total $\div$ that year's population; intervention totals reconcile to the all-clinical totals by year. \costcaveat}

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} clinical cost workbook (\texttt{indonesia\_model\_cost\_value\_formulae.xlsx}, sheet \texttt{Annual\_Cost}); all-clinical scenario, \textbf{undiscounted} additional cost by intervention (shared components counted once); population is the workbook's own \texttt{national\_population}. \textbf{Method (undiscounted):} coverage scales up over `r HZ_START`--`r HZ_END`; left is cumulative \textbf{undiscounted} additional cost through each year, right is that total $\div$ that year's population (`r price_year` US\$); intervention totals reconcile to the all-clinical undiscounted totals by year. \costcaveat}

```{r tbl-ph-ce, results='asis'}
                  "Reduction in that\nprobability, 2050","Deaths reduction\n2050","Cost per\ndeath averted",

  if (!is.na(ft$agg_idx)) k <- k |> row_spec(ft$agg_idx, bold=TRUE, background="#E7F4F1")
```

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} public-health cost workbook (\texttt{indonesia\_cost\_value\_public\_health\_formulae.xlsx}); annual additional cost reproduced from its \texttt{Annual\_Cost} inputs and reconciled to the run total; population is the workbook's own \texttt{national\_population}. \textbf{Method:} cumulative deaths averted `r HZ_START`--`r HZ_END` vs baseline; tobacco and sodium packages each modelled as one joint run. \textbf{Avg. annual additional cost per capita, 2026--`r HZ_END`} $=$ cumulative discounted additional cost over 2026--`r HZ_END` $\div$ (25 $\times$ `r HZ_START+1L` population); \textbf{cost per capita in `r HZ_END`} $=$ discounted additional cost in `r HZ_END` $\div$ `r HZ_END` population. \costcaveat}

## Even undiscounted, population policies avert deaths at very low cost

```{r tbl-ph-ce-undisc, results='asis'}
## Undiscounted counterpart of tbl-ph-ce: identical health columns; every monetary
## column undiscounted (annual undiscounted cost reproduced from the PH workbook's own
## Annual_Cost inputs and reconciled to the run's undiscounted total).
ftu <- family_table(met_ph, ph_all_id, ce_row_undisc)
if (nrow(ftu$tb)) {
  k <- kbl(ftu$tb, format="latex", booktabs=TRUE, escape=FALSE,
      col.names=mkhdr(c("Public-health policy","Deaths averted\n(cumulative)","Prob. of CVD death\nbefore age 70, 2050",
                  "Reduction in that\nprobability, 2050","Deaths reduction\n2050","Cost per death\naverted (undisc.)",
                  "Avg. annual add'l\ncost/capita, 2026-50 (undisc.)","Add'l cost/capita\nin 2050 (undisc.)")),
      align="lrrrrrrr") |>
    kable_styling(latex_options=c("hold_position","scale_down"), font_size=8.5) |>
    column_spec(1, bold=TRUE) |> row_spec(0, bold=TRUE)
  if (!is.na(ftu$agg_idx)) k <- k |> row_spec(ftu$agg_idx, bold=TRUE, background="#E7F4F1")
  print(k)
  reg_tbl("tbl-ph-ce-undisc",
          "Even undiscounted, population policies avert deaths at very low cost",
          ftu$tb,
          c("Public-health policy","Deaths averted\n(cumulative)","Prob. of CVD death\nbefore age 70, 2050",
            "Reduction in that\nprobability, 2050","Deaths reduction\n2050","Cost per death\naverted (undisc.)",
            "Avg. annual add'l\ncost/capita, 2026-50 (undisc.)","Add'l cost/capita\nin 2050 (undisc.)"))
  if (ftu$n_omitted > 0)
    cat(sprintf("\n\n\\vspace{1pt}\\scriptsize %d additional public-health intervention(s) omitted for space; see the appendix crosswalk and the workbook.\n", ftu$n_omitted))
} else cat("\\begin{center}\\large No public-health policies selected for this run.\\end{center}")
```

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} public-health cost workbook (\texttt{indonesia\_cost\_value\_public\_health\_formulae.xlsx}); annual additional cost reproduced from its \texttt{Annual\_Cost} inputs and reconciled to the run's \textbf{undiscounted} total; population is the workbook's own \texttt{national\_population}. \textbf{Method (undiscounted):} cumulative deaths averted `r HZ_START`--`r HZ_END` vs baseline; tobacco and sodium packages each modelled as one joint run. \textbf{Avg. annual additional cost per capita, 2026--`r HZ_END`} $=$ cumulative \textbf{undiscounted} additional cost over 2026--`r HZ_END` $\div$ (25 $\times$ `r HZ_START+1L` population); \textbf{cost per capita in `r HZ_END`} $=$ \textbf{undiscounted} additional cost in `r HZ_END` $\div$ `r HZ_END` population (`r price_year` US\$). Health results are identical to the discounted slide. \costcaveat}


# A stronger care cascade: the 70-30-30 to 70-70-70 strategy

## The cascade scale-up is ambitious but staged

\footnotesize Hypertension and type-2 diabetes are modelled with \textbf{diagnosed $\rightarrow$ treated $\rightarrow$ controlled} care cascades; \textbf{cholesterol} treatment coverage follows hypertension coverage. Coverage rises in two stages, then holds.

\vspace{1pt}
\begin{columns}[T]
\begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
\begin{clinicalblock}{Two staged milestones}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}\itemsep1pt
  \item \textbf{`r casc_ytar1` --- 70-30-30:} `r fmt_pct(casc_diag*100,0)` diagnosed, `r fmt_pct(casc_t30*100,0)` of those treated, `r fmt_pct(casc_c30*100,0)` of those controlled.
  \item \textbf{`r casc_ytar2` --- 70-70-70:} `r fmt_pct(casc_diag*100,0)` diagnosed, `r fmt_pct(casc_t40*100,0)` treated, `r fmt_pct(casc_c40*100,0)` controlled; held through `r casc_y1`.
  \item Linear scale-up from the observed baseline; coverage already above a milestone is \textbf{not scaled down}.
\end{itemize}
\end{clinicalblock}
\end{column}
\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
\begin{combinedblock}{Shares of all people with the condition}
\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
 & \textbf{`r casc_ytar1`} & \textbf{`r casc_ytar2`}\\
\midrule
Diagnosed  & `r fmt_pct(casc_diag*100,0)` & `r fmt_pct(casc_diag*100,0)`\\
Treated    & `r fmt_pct(casc_diag*casc_t30*100,0)` & `r fmt_pct(casc_diag*casc_t40*100,0)`\\
Controlled & `r fmt_pct(casc_diag*casc_t30*casc_c30*100,1)` & `r fmt_pct(casc_diag*casc_t40*casc_c40*100,1)`\\
\end{tabular}\\[3pt]
{\scriptsize treated $=70\%\times\{30,70\}\%$; controlled $=$ treated $\times\{30,70\}\%$.}
\end{combinedblock}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

\vspace{1pt}
\footnotesize \textbf{Effective modelled coverage} $=$ controlled $+\tfrac{1}{2}\times$ treated-but-uncontrolled $=$ \textbf{`r fmt_pct(casc_eff30*100,2)`} (`r casc_ytar1`) and \textbf{`r fmt_pct(casc_eff40*100,2)`} (`r casc_ytar2`): full effect to controlled patients, half to treated-but-uncontrolled.

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} cascade workbook (\texttt{Cascade\_Assumptions}, \texttt{Cascade\_Trajectory}); isolated runner; NCD-RisC coverage inputs. \textbf{Method:} nested targets on the diagnosed/treated/controlled shares; piecewise-linear scale-up, no backsliding.}

## Indonesia's hypertension cascade can progress in two achievable stages

```{r fig-htn-cascade, fig.width=9.4, fig.height=3.7, out.width="0.94\\linewidth"}
#Patch: manual update to Farizals value automatize later

htn_sh[year == 2025, `:=`(
  controlled = 0.04,
  treated    = 0.22,

)]

htn_sh[year == 2030, `:=`(

  treated    = 0.21,
  diagnosed  = 0.700
)]

htn_sh[year == 2040, `:=`(

  treated    = 0.490,
  diagnosed  = 0.700
)]


htn_long <- melt(htn_sh[, .(year, Diagnosed = diagnosed, Treated = treated, Controlled = controlled)],
                 id.vars = "year", variable.name = "stage", value.name = "share")
htn_long <- htn_long[!is.na(share)]
htn_long[, stage := factor(stage, levels = c("Diagnosed","Treated","Controlled"))]
htn_long[, xlab := factor(year, levels = c(HZ_START, casc_ytar1, casc_ytar2),

  theme_exec(11) +

"fig-htn-cascade", "Indonesia's hypertension cascade can progress in two achievable stages", 9.4, 3.7)
```

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} cascade \texttt{Cascade\_Trajectory} (sex-averaged) and \texttt{Cascade\_Assumptions}; scale-up begins `r HZ_START+1L`. \textbf{Method:} baseline (`r HZ_START`) shows only measured treated/controlled --- diagnosis is not modelled at baseline, so no diagnosed bar. Type-2 diabetes follows the same targets (baseline treated $\approx$ `r fmt_pct(dm_base$treated*100,1)`, controlled $\approx$ `r fmt_pct(dm_base$controlled*100,1)`).}

## Stronger prevention lowers premature deaths at a rising but bounded cost

```{r fig-casc-2panel, fig.width=9.6, fig.height=3.7, out.width="\\linewidth"}
lab_q  <- c(baseline = "Baseline (current course)", cascade = "Intervention")
qdat <- copy(casc_q)[, series := ifelse(scenario == "baseline", "Baseline (current course)", "Intervention")]
qdat[, panel := "Probability of death from CVD before age 70 (%)"]
setnames(qdat, "q", "value")
cdat <- rbind(
  casc_cost[, .(year, series = "Baseline (current course)", value = cum_base / 1e9)],
  casc_cost[, .(year, series = "Intervention",              value = cum_scen / 1e9)])
cdat[, panel := "Cumulative discounted health-system cost (US$ billions)"]
two <- rbind(qdat[, .(year, series, value, panel)], cdat)
two[, panel := factor(panel, levels = c("Probability of death from CVD before age 70 (%)",
                                         "Cumulative discounted health-system cost (US$ billions)"))]
casc_pal <- c("Baseline (current course)" = col_baseline, "Intervention" = "#D55E00")
ends <- two[, .SD[year == max(year)], by = .(series, panel)]
## Readable endpoint labels: short text, visible leader segments, and ample right-side
## room so labels never sit on the lines or clip. Deterministic (fixed seed + offsets).
ends[, lab := ifelse(series == "Intervention", "Intervention", "Baseline")]
reg_fig(
ggplot(two, aes(year, value, colour = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.15) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = ends, aes(label = lab), size = 2.7, fontface = "bold",
                           hjust = 0, nudge_x = 1.6, direction = "y",
                           segment.colour = "grey55", segment.size = 0.3,
                           min.segment.length = 0, box.padding = 0.5, point.padding = 0.3,
                           max.overlaps = Inf, seed = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = casc_pal) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(HZ_START, casc_y1 + 11), breaks = seq(HZ_START, casc_y1, 5)) +
  labs(title = NULL, x = "Year", y = NULL) +
  theme_exec(11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", colour = col_wbnavy, size = 10),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.25)),
"fig-casc-2panel", "Stronger prevention lowers premature deaths at a rising but bounded cost", 9.6, 3.7)
```

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} cascade workbook --- annual probability-of-death sheet (R-reconciled) and \texttt{Annual\_Cost}, cumulatively summed and reconciled to \texttt{Budget\_Impact}. \textbf{Method:} probability over the six CVD causes, ages 30--70; cumulative discounted health-system cost (`r fmt_pct(casc_disc*100,0)`/yr to `r HZ_START`, `r casc_price` US\$) of the CVD primary-care and type-2 diabetes cascades. \costcaveat}

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} cascade workbook --- annual probability-of-death sheet (R-reconciled) and \texttt{Annual\_Cost}, cumulatively summed and reconciled to \texttt{Budget\_Impact} \textbf{undiscounted} cumulative additional cost. \textbf{Method:} probability over the six CVD causes, ages 30--70 (identical to the discounted slide); cumulative \textbf{undiscounted} health-system cost (`r casc_price` US\$) of the CVD primary-care and type-2 diabetes cascades. \costcaveat}

## `r title_cascade_results`

```{r tbl-cascade, results='asis'}
snp <- lapply(casc_tab_years, casc_snapshot); names(snp) <- as.character(casc_tab_years)
mm  <- function(x) formatC(x / 1e6, format = "f", digits = 3, big.mark = ",")   # deaths, millions
bn  <- function(x) formatC(x / 1e9, format = "f", digits = 2)                    # cost, US$ billions
pcf <- function(x) paste0("US\\$", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2, big.mark = ",")) # US$/person
casc_tb <- data.table(
  Metric = c("\\quad Baseline (current course)", "\\quad Intervention",
             "\\quad Baseline (current course)", "\\quad Intervention",
             "Additional cost (US\\$ billion, discounted)", "Deaths prevented (million)",
             "Additional cost per capita in that year (US\\$, discounted)"),
  y1 = c(mm(snp[[1]]$d_base), mm(snp[[1]]$d_scen), bn(snp[[1]]$c_base), bn(snp[[1]]$c_scen), bn(snp[[1]]$c_add), mm(snp[[1]]$d_av), pcf(snp[[1]]$pc_ann)),
  y2 = c(mm(snp[[2]]$d_base), mm(snp[[2]]$d_scen), bn(snp[[2]]$c_base), bn(snp[[2]]$c_scen), bn(snp[[2]]$c_add), mm(snp[[2]]$d_av), pcf(snp[[2]]$pc_ann)),
  y3 = c(mm(snp[[3]]$d_base), mm(snp[[3]]$d_scen), bn(snp[[3]]$c_base), bn(snp[[3]]$c_scen), bn(snp[[3]]$c_add), mm(snp[[3]]$d_av), pcf(snp[[3]]$pc_ann)))
reg_tbl("tbl-cascade", title_cascade_results, casc_tb,
        c("Cumulative from 2025 through year (unless noted)", as.character(casc_tab_years)))
kbl(casc_tb, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c("Cumulative from 2025 through year (unless noted)", as.character(casc_tab_years)),
    align = "lrrr") |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"), font_size = 8) |>
  column_spec(1, width = "6.6cm") |> column_spec(2:4, width = "2.2cm") |>
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE) |>
  pack_rows("Projected deaths --- CVD (six causes) + type-2 diabetes (million)", 1, 2, bold = TRUE, latex_gap_space = "0.2em", escape = FALSE) |>
  pack_rows("Projected health-system cost (US\\$ billion, discounted)", 3, 4, bold = TRUE, latex_gap_space = "0.2em", escape = FALSE) |>
  pack_rows("Net effect of the strategy", 5, 6, bold = TRUE, latex_gap_space = "0.2em") |>
  pack_rows("Annual financing intensity (that year only, not cumulative)", 7, 7, bold = TRUE, latex_gap_space = "0.2em", escape = FALSE)
```

## The care cascade and tobacco policies jointly move Indonesia further toward its neighbours

```{r fig-40q30-cascade, fig.width=8.0, fig.height=6.0, out.width="\\linewidth"}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## FIVE EXPLICITLY-MODELLED annual probability-of-death-before-70 trajectories,
## each read as the stored R-reconciled literal (cvd_40q30_r) from its OWN
## workbook's CVD_40q30 sheet -- never summed, multiplied, averaged, or
## interpolated. All source workbooks' baselines reconcile EXACTLY (asserted below),
## so the six-cause / exact-ages-30-70 definition is identical and the lines are
## directly comparable:
## * Hypertension/cholesterol + diabetes 70-70-70 cascade
##     -> S_70_30_30_TO_70_70_70 (joint cascade + public-health wb)
## * 70-70-70 cascade + tobacco tax ONLY (targeted interaction; the tobacco tax
##   is the ONLY public-health intervention added -- NOT clean-air, mass-media or
##   the advertising ban, and NOT the full all_cascade_public_health package)
##     -> S_70_30_30_TO_70_70_70_I_PH_TOBACCO_TAX (joint cascade + public-health wb)
## * Tobacco tax -> I_PH_TOBACCO_TAX (public-health wb)
## * All public-health interventions -> ph_all_id (all_public_health, public-health wb)
## * All clinical + public health -> all_clinical_public_health (combined wb)
## The all-public-health line is read as the public-health workbook's OWN
## all-public-health scenario (its stored annual cvd_40q30_r) -- NOT reused from the
## combined workbook, NOT summed from individual policies, NOT the tobacco-tax line.
## Reuses the SAME observed history (idn_obs) and ASEAN comparators (cmp_lines)
## as the earlier neighbours slide; the modelled status-quo baseline is NOT drawn.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
scen_specs <- list(
  list(id = "S_70_30_30_TO_70_70_70", wb = casc_ph_wb,
       label = "70-70-70 target achieved",
       col = col_clinical),
  list(id = "S_70_30_30_TO_70_70_70_I_PH_TOBACCO_TAX", wb = casc_ph_wb,
       label = "70-70-70 target achieved + tobacco tax",
       col = "#7B3294"),
  list(id = "all_clinical_public_health", wb = wb_comb, label = "All clinical + tobacco tax & regulatory package", col = col_combined)
)

read_scen_q3 <- function(path, sid) {
  d <- rd(path, "CVD_40q30")
  if ("location" %in% names(d)) d <- d[location == "Indonesia"]
  qc <- if ("cvd_40q30_r" %in% names(d)) "cvd_40q30_r" else "cvd_40q30"
  d[scenario == sid & year >= HZ_START & !is.na(get(qc)), .(year, q = get(qc))][order(year)]
}

idn_scen5 <- rbindlist(lapply(scen_specs, function(s) {
  x <- read_scen_q3(s$wb, s$id)
  x[, `:=`(scenario = s$id, scen = s$label)]
  x[]
}))

## Fail loudly if any requested scenario lacks a full HZ_START..HZ_END trajectory.
for (s in scen_specs) {
  ys <- idn_scen5[scenario == s$id, year]
  if (!length(ys) || max(ys) < HZ_END || min(ys) > HZ_START)
    stop(sprintf("VALIDATION STOP -- scenario '%s' has no full %d-%d trajectory in %s",
                 s$id, HZ_START, HZ_END, basename(s$wb)), call. = FALSE)
}

## Baseline reconciliation: every plotted line's own workbook must share the identical
## six-cause / ages-30-70 baseline probability series across HZ_START..HZ_END, so the
## five lines are directly comparable.
.base_ref <- read_scen_q3(wb_comb, "baseline")
for (s in scen_specs) {
  .b <- read_scen_q3(s$wb, "baseline")
  .bm <- merge(.base_ref, .b, by = "year")
  if (nrow(.bm) < length(HZ_START:HZ_END) || max(abs(.bm$q.x - .bm$q.y)) > 1e-6)
    stop(sprintf("VALIDATION STOP -- baseline probability series in %s does not reconcile with the combined workbook baseline",
                 basename(s$wb)), call. = FALSE)
}

scen5_levels <- vapply(scen_specs, `[[`, character(1), "label")
idn_scen5[, scen := factor(scen, levels = scen5_levels)]
scen5_pal <- setNames(vapply(scen_specs, `[[`, character(1), "col"), scen5_levels)

## Endpoint labels ONLY for ASEAN comparators (right-hand side).
## Scenario (intervention) labels are deliberately omitted from the RHS;
## they appear only in the legend.
cmp_end <- cmp_lines[, .SD[which.max(year)], by = country_label][
  , .(year, q, country_label)]

p_fig_40q30_cascade <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(
    data = cmp_lines,
    aes(year, q, group = country_label),
    colour = col_comparator,
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = idn_obs,
    aes(year, q),
    colour = "grey20",
    linewidth = 1.0
  ) +
  annotate(
    "segment",
    x = 2024, xend = 2024, y = 10.5, yend = 20.5,
    linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey45"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 2024, y = 20.9,
    label = "Modeled scenarios →",
    hjust = 1, size = 2.7, colour = "grey35"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = idn_scen5,
    aes(year, q, colour = scen),
    linewidth = 1.15,
    linetype = "22"
  ) +
  ## Country names only (larger, grey) on the right-hand side
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data = cmp_end,
    aes(year, q, label = country_label),
    colour = "grey40",
    size = 3.4,
    hjust = 0,
    nudge_x = 1.3,
    direction = "y",
    segment.colour = "grey65",
    segment.size = 0.25,
    min.segment.length = 0,
    box.padding = 0.35,
    point.padding = 0.2,
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    show.legend = FALSE,
    seed = 11
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = scen5_pal,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(1995, 2068),
    breaks = seq(1995, 2050, 5),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(
    title = "Cascade, tobacco policies, and combined packages",
    subtitle = "Chance of dying from CVD between exact ages 30 and 70",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Probability of CVD death before age 70 (%)"
    ) +
  theme_exec(11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.02, 0.02),   # lower-left
    legend.justification = c(0, 0),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = alpha("white", 0.85), colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.key.width = unit(1.1, "cm"),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.40, "cm"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7.8),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.25)
  )

reg_fig(p_fig_40q30_cascade,
        "fig-40q30-cascade",
        "The care cascade and tobacco policies jointly move Indonesia further toward its neighbours",
        8.0, 6.0)
```

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} each modelled line is the stored R-reconciled literal from the annual probability-of-death-before-70 sheet of its \emph{own} workbook --- \textbf{70-70-70 hypertension/cholesterol + diabetes cascade} and \textbf{cascade + tobacco tax:} joint cascade/public-health workbook \texttt{indonesia\_model\_cost\_value\_70\_30\_30\_to\_70\_70\_70\_public\_health\_formulae.xlsx} (scenarios \texttt{S\_70\_30\_30\_TO\_70\_70\_70} and \texttt{S\_70\_30\_30\_TO\_70\_70\_70\_I\_PH\_TOBACCO\_TAX}); \textbf{Tobacco tax:} public-health workbook \texttt{indonesia\_cost\_value\_public\_health\_formulae.xlsx} (scenario \texttt{I\_PH\_TOBACCO\_TAX}); \textbf{All public-health interventions:} the SAME public-health workbook (scenario \texttt{all\_public\_health}); \textbf{All clinical and public-health interventions:} combined workbook \texttt{indonesia\_model\_cost\_value\_clinical\_public\_health\_formulae.xlsx} (scenario \texttt{all\_clinical\_public\_health}). ASEAN comparators in \texttt{data/raw/}. \textbf{Method:} every intervention line is a \emph{single joint model run} applying its listed interventions simultaneously --- never a sum, product, or average of separately modelled effects; all source workbooks share an identical baseline (asserted), so every line is the probability of death from the six modelled cardiovascular causes over exact ages 30--70. The plotted purple ``cascade + tobacco tax'' line (scenario \texttt{S\_70\_30\_30\_TO\_70\_70\_70\_I\_PH\_TOBACCO\_TAX}) adds ONLY the tobacco tax to the cascade --- it does NOT include the clean-air law, mass-media campaign, or advertising ban, and is NOT the broader \texttt{all\_cascade\_public\_health} package. Comparators are WPP-scaled reference series shown for context only.}

```{r fig-sub-pareto, fig.width=9.7, fig.height=3.5, out.width="\\linewidth"}
sf_scale <- max(da_prov$da)
reg_fig(
ggplot(da_prov, aes(x = location)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = da), fill = col_clinical, width = 0.72) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cum_share / 100 * sf_scale, group = 1), colour = col_casefatal, linewidth = 0.7) +

    labels = function(x) formatC(x / 1e3, format = "d", big.mark = ","),

    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / sf_scale * 100, name = "Cumulative share of national total (%)",
                        labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"))) +

  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.4, size = 5.6),
        axis.title.y.left  = element_text(colour = col_clinical, size = 8),

"fig-sub-pareto", title_sub_pareto, 9.7, 3.5)
```

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} isolated subnational cascade workbook (\texttt{...\_formulae\_subnational.xlsx}), sheet \texttt{Health\_Outcomes}. \textbf{Method:} bars are cumulative deaths averted `r HZ_START`--`r HZ_END` per province (official cascade scope: six CVD causes $+$ type-2 diabetes); the line is the running share of the national total. Province-summed baseline deaths reconcile to \texttt{Province\_Reconciliation} (`r sub_recon_status`; residual `r fmt_pct(sub_recon_reldiff,2)`). `r sub_caveat` `r sub_hetero`}

## `r title_sub_cvddeath`

```{r fig-sub-cvddeath, fig.width=9.4, fig.height=3.0, out.width="\\linewidth"}
## % reduction in CVD deaths: aggregate summed baseline & scenario CVD deaths to the
## boundary polygon, then recompute the reduction (never average percentages).
cvd_map <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(sub_ytar1, sub_ytar2), function(yr) {
  d <- merge(cvd_red[year == yr], prov_meta[, .(location, iso)], by = "location")
  a <- d[, .(base = sum(base), scen = sum(scen)), by = iso]
  a[, value := (base - scen) / base * 100]
  s <- map_sf(a[, .(iso, value)]); s$panel <- as.character(yr); s
}))
cvd_lims <- pos_scale_lims(cvd_map$value)   # bar starts at the min positive displayed value
reg_fig(
ggplot(cvd_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = value), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.12) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = ramp_grn, limits = cvd_lims, oob = scales::squish,
                       labels = function(x) paste0(formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1), "%"),
                       name = "Reduction in CVD deaths vs baseline (%)") +
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
  theme_map_exec(10),
"fig-sub-cvddeath", title_sub_cvddeath, 9.4, 3.0)
```

## `r title_sub_cost_undisc`

```{r fig-sub-cost-undisc, fig.width=9.4, fig.height=3.0, out.width="\\linewidth"}
## Undiscounted counterpart of fig-sub-cost: each province's ANNUAL UNDISCOUNTED
## additional cost / that province's population (sum(cost)/sum(pop) per boundary
## polygon), for the two milestone years. Same geometry, same common positive-anchored
## legend rule (zeros squished to the low colour, no detached US$0 tick).
cost_map_u <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(sub_ytar1, sub_ytar2), function(yr) {
  d <- merge(cost_prov_u[year == yr], prov_meta[, .(location, iso)], by = "location")
  a <- d[, .(value = sum(undisc) / sum(pop)), by = iso]
  s <- map_sf(a); s$panel <- as.character(yr); s
}))
cost_lims_u <- pos_scale_lims(cost_map_u$value)
reg_fig(
ggplot(cost_map_u) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = value), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.12) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = ramp_org, limits = cost_lims_u, oob = scales::squish,
                       breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 4),
                       labels = function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2),
                       name = "Annual additional cost per capita (US$ per person, undiscounted)") +
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
  theme_map_exec(10),
"fig-sub-cost-undisc", title_sub_cost_undisc, 9.4, 3.0)
```

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} subnational cascade workbook, sheets \texttt{Annual\_Cost} / \texttt{Budget\_Impact}. \textbf{Method (undiscounted):} \emph{annual} (not cumulative) \textbf{undiscounted} additional cost in each province divided by that province's population, for `r sub_ytar1` and `r sub_ytar2` (`r sub_price` US\$); one common scale. `r sub_geo_note` `r sub_caveat` `r sub_hetero`}

# What this means for policy

## Prevention and clinical care together offer the biggest, most affordable gains

\begin{columns}[T]

```{r impl-right, results='asis'}
  cat(sprintf("  \\item \\textbf{The premature-mortality target is within reach.} The combined package bends Indonesia's probability of death from CVD before age 70 down by about %s by %d.\n", fmt_pct(combo_qred,0), HZ_END))
```

\end{itemize}

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} results contract (\texttt{09\_deck\_results.rds}); cascade workbook. \textbf{Method:} interpretation of modelled deaths averted, premature-mortality reduction, and cost per death averted; policy translation needs judgement on feasibility, financing, and delivery. \costcaveat}

## What these results can and cannot tell us

\begin{itemize}\footnotesize\itemsep3pt
  \item Results depend on \textbf{modelled epidemiological estimates} (GBD) and calibration; the real burden may differ.
  \item \textbf{Effect sizes, future coverage, and unit costs are uncertain}; interventions are assumed to reach and sustain their targets.
  \item The disease model is \textbf{simplified} (healthy $\to$ living with CVD $\to$ death; no recovery; no comorbidity interactions).
  \item Value for money is expressed as \textbf{cost per death averted}; effects on illness (morbidity) and productivity are not valued in money here.
  \item \textbf{Costing results are preliminary.} Unit costs, service use, and delivery assumptions require further validation against \textbf{BPJS and Ministry of Health} data before policy use.
  \item Projections are \textbf{scenarios, not forecasts or guarantees}; they show what is achievable if interventions are delivered as modelled.
\end{itemize}

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} Indonesia CVD model and its input workbooks (GBD 2023; UN WPP 2024; FAIR Choices effects; programme and policy unit costs). \textbf{Method:} qualitative statement of the assumptions and uncertainties that bound the quantitative results above.}

# Technical appendix

## Appendix 1 --- Scenario crosswalk

```{r tbl-crosswalk}
## Built dynamically from the current run's combined-workbook scenarios.
fam_order <- c(clinical = 1, public_health = 2, clinical_public_health = 3)
xwd <- copy(met_comb)[, .(scenario, intervention_family, scenario_label, n_interventions)]
xwd[, ford := fam_order[intervention_family]]
xwd[is.na(ford), ford := 9]
setorder(xwd, ford, -n_interventions)
fam_disp <- c(clinical = "Clinical (FAIR Choices)", public_health = "Public health",
              clinical_public_health = "Combined")
xwd[, Family := fam_disp[intervention_family]]
xwd[is.na(Family), Family := intervention_family]
## Only show the family label on its first row (visual grouping).

reg_tbl("tbl-crosswalk", "Appendix 1 - Scenario crosswalk", xw,

  kable_styling(latex_options=c("hold_position"), font_size=5.2) |>
  column_spec(1, bold=TRUE, width="3.0cm") |> column_spec(2, monospace=TRUE, width="4.0cm") |>
```

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} combined workbook \texttt{Scenario\_Catalog} (binding active-scenario contract). \textbf{Method:} identity/labels/family read from the current run; excluded interventions never appear; packages are single joint runs of their children (omitted from main tables to avoid double-counting).}

## Appendix 2 --- Definitions, horizons and assumptions

\footnotesize
\begin{columns}[T]
\begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
\textbf{Metrics}
\begin{itemize}\scriptsize\itemsep2pt
  \item \textbf{Deaths averted (cumulative)} $=\sum_{t=`r HZ_START`}^{`r HZ_END`}(\text{baseline deaths}_t-\text{scenario deaths}_t)$, across modelled CVD \& diabetes causes.
  \item \textbf{\% reduction in deaths, `r HZ_END`} $=100\times(\text{baseline}-\text{scenario})/\text{baseline}$ in `r HZ_END`.
  \item \textbf{Probability of death from CVD before age 70} $=$ probability of dying of CVD between exact ages 30 and 70 (six CVD causes, both sexes, single-year life table).
  \item \textbf{\% reduction in that probability, `r HZ_END`}: analogous to deaths.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}
\begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
\textbf{Costing \& value for money}
\begin{itemize}\scriptsize\itemsep2pt
  \item Horizon `r HZ_START`--`r HZ_END`; cost discount rate `r fmt_pct(disc_rate*100,0)`/yr; price year `r price_year`.
  \item Costs in \textbf{market US\$}; cost perspective: `r cost_perspective`.
  \item \textbf{Cost per death averted} $=$ cumulative \textbf{discounted} additional (incremental) cost $\div$ cumulative \textbf{undiscounted} deaths averted.
  \item A ``Dominant'' scenario averts deaths while lowering cost; ``not defined'' means no deaths averted.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

\vspace{3pt}
\scriptsize \textbf{Model.} Discrete-time state-transition model; single-year ages 0--95; six CVD causes (IHD, ischemic stroke, intracerebral haemorrhage, hypertensive heart disease, rheumatic heart disease, cardiomyopathy \& myocarditis) plus type-2 diabetes; calibrated to GBD 2023; demography and life expectancy from UN WPP 2024. \textbf{Data provenance:} every ordinary-run number is read from the current-run results contract (\texttt{output/09\_deck\_results.rds}) and the workbooks' literal probability-of-death series; the cascade strategy is read from its isolated workbook; scenario identity follows the \texttt{Scenario\_Catalog} contract (binding \texttt{include\_flag}). No Excel recalculation is used.

## Appendix 3 --- How costs are calculated

\footnotesize Intervention-based costing adapted from the DCP Cost Model of @Watkins2020ResourceRequirements, from a `r cost_perspective` perspective with annual projections. For intervention $i$, sex/age group $s$, year $t$:

\vspace{-2pt}
\begin{columns}[T]
\begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
{\scriptsize
\begin{align*}
C_{i,s,t} &= PIN_{i,s,t}\times cov_{i,s,t}\times f_i\times uc_i\\[2pt]
\Delta C_{s,t} &= C_{s,t}-C_{0,t}\\[2pt]
PV(\Delta C_s) &= \sum_{t=`r HZ_START+1L`}^{`r HZ_END`}\frac{\Delta C_{s,t}}{(1+r)^{\,t-`r HZ_START`}}\\[2pt]
\text{Cost per death prevented}_s &= \frac{PV(\Delta C_s)}{\sum_{t=`r HZ_START+1L`}^{`r HZ_END`}(D_{0,t}-D_{s,t})}
\end{align*}}
\end{column}
\begin{column}{0.46\textwidth}
\scriptsize
$PIN$ = people in need (population $\times$ epidemiological need); $cov$ = coverage (baseline or scenario); $f_i$ = services per person per year; $uc_i$ = Indonesia-adjusted unit cost; subscript $0$ = baseline (current course), $s$ = scenario; $r$ = `r fmt_pct(disc_rate*100,0)`/yr discount rate; price year `r price_year`; currency market US\$; perspective `r cost_perspective`. Deaths $D$ remain \textbf{undiscounted} in the cost-per-death calculation. Downstream cost offsets are \textbf{excluded}.
\end{column}
\end{columns}

\srcmethod{\textbf{Source:} adapted from Watkins et al. (2020); unit costs, coverage, and people-in-need from the input workbooks and \texttt{Annual\_Cost}; demography from UN WPP 2024. \textbf{Method:} annual costs by intervention $\times$ group $\times$ year, differenced against baseline, discounted to the `r HZ_START` base year. \costcaveat}

## Appendix 4 --- References

\scriptsize

::: {#refs}
:::

```{r build-xlsx-workbook, include=FALSE}
## =====================================================================
##  ASSEMBLE + WRITE THE COMPANION WORKBOOK: reports/executive_slides.xlsx
##  Runs after every slide chunk, so .xlsx_items holds every figure and
##  table captured (in slide order) by reg_fig()/reg_tbl(). Each item gets
##  its own logically-named worksheet (<=31 chars) labelled with the slide
##  title and the chunk/figure/table id; tables are written as real,
##  editable cells; figures are embedded as PNG images at readable
##  resolution. A leading Contents sheet indexes everything.
##
##  Wrapped in tryCatch so a workbook hiccup can never break the deck:
##  the slide PDF is the primary artifact and its rendering is untouched.
## =====================================================================
if (isTRUE(.xlsx_enabled) && length(.xlsx_items)) tryCatch({

  xlsx_out <- here::here("reports", "executive_slides.xlsx")

  ## ---- Strip LaTeX markup from a string so cells/labels are plain text ----
  latex_clean <- function(x) {
    x <- as.character(x); x[is.na(x)] <- ""
    ## \textcolor{colour}{text} -> text (two braced args; keep the second)
    x <- gsub("\\\\textcolor\\{[^{}]*\\}\\{([^{}]*)\\}", "\\1", x)
    x <- gsub("\\\\makecell\\[[^]]*\\]\\{([^{}]*)\\}", "\\1", x)
    ## remaining single-argument commands \cmd{...} -> ... (iterate for nesting)
    repeat { y <- gsub("\\\\[A-Za-z@]+\\*?\\{([^{}]*)\\}", "\\1", x); if (identical(y, x)) break; x <- y }
    ## escaped specials
    x <- gsub("US\\\\\\$", "US$", x)
    x <- gsub("\\\\%", "%", x); x <- gsub("\\\\\\$", "$", x)
    x <- gsub("\\\\_", "_", x); x <- gsub("\\\\&", "&", x); x <- gsub("\\\\#", "#", x)
    x <- gsub("\\$\\\\approx\\$", "~", x)
    x <- gsub("\\\\textasciitilde\\{\\}", "~", x)
    ## any leftover backslash commands (no braces) then stray braces
    x <- gsub("\\\\[A-Za-z@]+", "", x); x <- gsub("[{}]", "", x)
    ## header line breaks -> spaces; collapse whitespace
    x <- gsub("[\r\n]+", " ", x); x <- gsub("[ \t]+", " ", x)
    trimws(x)
  }
  ## ---- Sheet-name helper: Excel forbids \ / ? * [ ] : and caps at 31 chars --
  sanitize_sheet <- function(s) substr(gsub("[\\\\/?*\\[\\]:]", "-", s), 1, 31)

  ## openxlsx 4.2.x registers a drawing + vmlDrawing relationship (and a drawing
  ## Content_Types override) for EVERY worksheet, but writes drawing<i>.xml only for
  ## sheets that hold an image and never writes the vmlDrawing parts -- leaving
  ## dangling part references that Excel tolerates but strict readers (openpyxl /
  ## LibreOffice / Sheets) reject. Remove ONLY the phantom references, keeping the
  ## real embedded-image drawings intact. Guarded no-op on a future openxlsx layout.
  strip_phantom_drawings <- function(wb) {
    tryCatch({
      has_img <- vapply(seq_along(wb$worksheets),
                        function(i) !is.null(wb$drawings[[i]]) && length(wb$drawings[[i]]) > 0, logical(1))
      if (!is.null(wb$Content_Types)) {
        is_draw  <- grepl("/xl/drawings/drawing[0-9]+\\.xml", wb$Content_Types)
        keep_pat <- if (any(has_img))
          paste0("PartName=\"/xl/drawings/drawing", which(has_img), "\\.xml\"", collapse = "|") else NA_character_
        keep_img <- if (is.na(keep_pat)) rep(FALSE, length(wb$Content_Types)) else grepl(keep_pat, wb$Content_Types)
        wb$Content_Types <- wb$Content_Types[!is_draw | keep_img]
      }
      if (!is.null(wb$worksheets_rels))
        for (i in seq_along(wb$worksheets_rels)) {
          r <- wb$worksheets_rels[[i]]; if (!length(r)) next
          r <- r[!grepl("/vmlDrawing", r)]                       # vmlDrawing parts are never written
          if (!has_img[i]) r <- r[!grepl("/drawings/drawing[0-9]+\\.xml", r)]
          wb$worksheets_rels[[i]] <- r
        }
    }, error = function(e) message("  (phantom-drawing strip skipped: ", conditionMessage(e), ")"))
    invisible(wb)
  }

  wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
  st_title <- openxlsx::createStyle(fontSize = 13, textDecoration = "bold", fontColour = "#0F2A56")
  st_sub   <- openxlsx::createStyle(fontSize = 9,  textDecoration = "italic", fontColour = "#5B6B7B")
  st_link  <- openxlsx::createStyle(fontColour = "#3B6FB6", textDecoration = "underline")
  st_hdr   <- openxlsx::createStyle(textDecoration = "bold", fgFill = "#EAF1FB",
                                    halign = "center", valign = "center", wrapText = TRUE,
                                    border = "TopBottom", borderColour = "#B7C7DA")
  st_ihdr  <- openxlsx::createStyle(textDecoration = "bold", fgFill = "#0F2A56", fontColour = "white")

  ## Pre-compute one worksheet name per item.
  item_sheets <- vapply(seq_along(.xlsx_items),
                        function(i) sanitize_sheet(sprintf("%02d_%s", i, .xlsx_items[[i]]$id)), character(1))

  ## ---- Contents / index sheet (added first => leftmost tab) ---------------
  openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, "Contents")
  openxlsx::writeData(wb, "Contents", "Executive deck - companion workbook", startCol = 1, startRow = 1)
  openxlsx::addStyle(wb, "Contents", st_title, rows = 1, cols = 1)
  openxlsx::writeData(wb, "Contents",
    sprintf("Every figure and table from executive_slides.Rmd, in slide order (generated %s).",
            format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")),
    startCol = 1, startRow = 2)
  openxlsx::addStyle(wb, "Contents", st_sub, rows = 2, cols = 1)
  contents <- data.frame(
    `#`            = seq_along(.xlsx_items),
    Type           = vapply(.xlsx_items, function(z) z$kind, character(1)),
    `Slide title`  = vapply(.xlsx_items, function(z) latex_clean(z$title), character(1)),
    Identifier     = vapply(.xlsx_items, function(z) z$id, character(1)),
    Worksheet      = item_sheets,
    check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  openxlsx::writeData(wb, "Contents", contents, startRow = 4, startCol = 1, colNames = TRUE)
  openxlsx::addStyle(wb, "Contents", st_ihdr, rows = 4, cols = seq_len(ncol(contents)), gridExpand = TRUE)
  openxlsx::setColWidths(wb, "Contents", cols = 1:5, widths = c(5, 9, 62, 26, 24))
  openxlsx::freezePane(wb, "Contents", firstActiveRow = 5)

  ## ---- One worksheet per item --------------------------------------------
  for (i in seq_along(.xlsx_items)) {
    it <- .xlsx_items[[i]]; sh <- item_sheets[i]
    openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, sh)
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, sh, latex_clean(it$title), startRow = 1, startCol = 1)
    openxlsx::addStyle(wb, sh, st_title, rows = 1, cols = 1)
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, sh, sprintf("%s  |  %s", toupper(it$kind), it$id), startRow = 2, startCol = 1)
    openxlsx::addStyle(wb, sh, st_sub, rows = 2, cols = 1)
    try({
      openxlsx::writeFormula(wb, sh,
        x = openxlsx::makeHyperlinkString(sheet = "Contents", row = 1, col = 1, text = "<- Contents"),
        startRow = 3, startCol = 1)
      openxlsx::addStyle(wb, sh, st_link, rows = 3, cols = 1)
    }, silent = TRUE)

    r0 <- 5L
    if (identical(it$kind, "table")) {
      df <- it$data
      ## Cleaned display headers: prefer the slide's own col_names, else the object's names.
      hdr <- if (!is.null(it$col_names) && length(it$col_names) == ncol(df))
               latex_clean(it$col_names) else latex_clean(names(df))
      names(df) <- make.unique(hdr)
      ## Clean every character/factor cell to plain text (LaTeX markup -> readable).
      for (j in seq_along(df))
        if (is.character(df[[j]]) || is.factor(df[[j]])) df[[j]] <- latex_clean(as.character(df[[j]]))
      openxlsx::writeData(wb, sh, df, startRow = r0, startCol = 1, colNames = TRUE, headerStyle = st_hdr)
      ## Readable, capped column widths.
      widths <- vapply(seq_along(df), function(j) {
        w <- max(nchar(names(df)[j]), max(nchar(as.character(df[[j]])), 0L, na.rm = TRUE))
        min(60, max(12, w + 2))
      }, numeric(1))
      openxlsx::setColWidths(wb, sh, cols = seq_along(df), widths = widths)
      openxlsx::freezePane(wb, sh, firstActiveRow = r0 + 1)
    } else {
      if (!is.na(it$path) && file.exists(it$path)) {
        openxlsx::insertImage(wb, sh, file = it$path, startRow = r0, startCol = 1,
                              width = it$width, height = it$height, units = "in", dpi = 200)
      } else {
        openxlsx::writeData(wb, sh, "[figure image could not be generated for this run]",
                            startRow = r0, startCol = 1)
      }
    }
  }

  strip_phantom_drawings(wb)
  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, xlsx_out, overwrite = TRUE)
  message(sprintf("Companion workbook written: %s  (%d items: %d figures, %d tables)",
                  xlsx_out, length(.xlsx_items),
                  sum(vapply(.xlsx_items, function(z) z$kind == "figure", logical(1))),
                  sum(vapply(.xlsx_items, function(z) z$kind == "table",  logical(1)))))
}, error = function(e)
  warning("Companion workbook (executive_slides.xlsx) was NOT written: ", conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE))
```
